identity.real_world_identity_notes: McLaren MP4/4, the Honda RA168E turbocharged car of the 1988 season, using a Weismann-McLaren six-speed manual gearbox.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift.

The gate is a dogleg, and the driver reports first at the bottom right rather than the bottom left, so the pattern is mirrored horizontally against every other dogleg in the dataset. The schema records the gate as dogleg-h, which is true of it, and the mirroring is kept here because no value expresses it.
Gearbox construction is not established. The source names Weismann-McLaren but not its engagement, so the downshift blip stays unknown rather than being inferred from racing practice.

Clutch telemetry was present while the running shifts were accepted as clutchless. The channel cannot separate the pedal from the clutch the car works itself, and this gearbox works its own on every shift, so the accepted results stand. The driver confirmed no pedal was used.

Only the high-downforce identity was observed. AMS2 selects the aero configuration from the circuit, so this car reports a different identity at a low-downforce track; that identity is not recorded here because it has not been observed and an exact match cannot be guessed.

Running shifts went through without the clutch while the gearbox provides no automatic cut or blip, so the driver shifts clutchlessly and supplies the lift and the blip. That combination is period-correct for a Formula One car of this era and is itself a sign of dog engagement: a dog box is routinely shifted without the clutch, where a synchronised gearbox resists it. It is recorded as a supporting observation, not as proof, and the gearbox type stays unknown until a source states the engagement.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.mclaren-honda-mp4-4-high-downforce.20260814t230415755z-357c0656 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the MP4/4 and its gearbox, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

Wikipedia gives a Weismann-McLaren 6-speed manual, and the live drive selected six H-pattern gears with no automatic cut or blip. The guided drive observed first at the bottom right of the gate, mirrored against the other doglegs in the dataset.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: Weismann-McLaren six-speed with a mirrored dogleg gate: first is down and to the right on this car, not the left as on every other dogleg here. Second through sixth then fall in one straight line.
